mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows Alloy to construct a world where two AuditEntries share the same (application, eventType) pair — an UPDATE-style overwrite. Both AppendOnly and FR_016_AuditAppendOnly require the pair to be unique; injecting a duplicate forces a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.application = e2.application and e1.eventType = e2.eventType }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows a customer to hold two simultaneous PendingReview applications, which violates FR-005 and the partial-unique-index invariant. The injection explicitly constructs this forbidden state, ensuring the predicate finds a counterexample.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OnePendingViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.owner = a2.owner and a1.status = PendingReview and a2.status = PendingReview }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the closed-world matrix assignment lets Alloy freely populate PermMatrix.Allowed. Adding Customer -> PostDecision directly violates the LeastPrivilege predicate (which asserts that cell is denied) and exposes the missing staff-only guard checked by FR_015_StaffOnlyDecisionAudit.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { Customer -> PostDecision in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows two Decision atoms to reference the same LoanApplication, modelling a race-condition win by two concurrent staff members. The injection forces exactly this forbidden state, causing all three assertions that prohibit dual decisions to find counterexamples.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DualDecisionViolation { some disj d1, d2: Decision | d1.application = d2.application }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that a Customer's GetApplicationByRef operation must target only their own application. The injection constructs a Customer operation that targets another customer's application, violating all three ownership/isolation/leakage assertions.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Customer and op.kind = GetApplicationByRef and (some op.targetApp) and op.targetApp.owner != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact allows AuditEntries to carry a misattributed actor — e.g., a Submitted event attributed to a BankStaff member, or an Approved event attributed to a Customer. The injection forces the most egregious misattribution (a Submitted event attributed to staff), which is caught by AttributionCorrectness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some e: AuditEntry | e.eventType = Submitted_E and e.actor.role = BankStaff }
